_doc: Private methods of the hand port, as compiler/oc/build.py reads them for a module's compiled override (installs override.private keys of these, refuses the others). The methods the hand port runs itself, through a handle of src/orm/dispatch_gen.ts (callPrivate), are in src/orm/dispatch_map.json, with their returns, above, kwargs and default_of described here (compiler/dispatch.py checks them); this file keeps covered, unreached and unported. The override runs around the hand port's whole implementation, so a definition of another module above it in the MRO (run after it in Odoo) must be one that does nothing wherever the hand port gets that far: `above` names them, with the reason. returns: what super() gives the compiled override (self: the records it was called on). covered: methods the hand port implements for every Community definition of them at once, so that an override from one of `modules` needs no compiled code (`reason` says why the result is Odoo's for any module set; compiler/private_hooks_check.py checks it against the source). unreached: methods no flow of the port can run (the hand port has no code for the model, and every caller in Odoo is a method of that model): an override needs no compiled code, as nothing calls it; compiler/private_hooks_check.py checks both; a site build that compiles a caller reaches it as compiled code instead. unported: methods the hand port has no implementation of (no registration, no callPrivate: a call from a report template or over RPC refuses as not registered), so an override needs no compiled code; compiler/private_hooks_check.py checks that worker/src registers or hooks no method of that name. default_of: the method is a field's default function (`default=_default_x`, fields.py:545 calls that function, not the method by name): the hand port's default runs it through callPrivate, and compiler/private_hooks_check.py checks that no Community or OCA code calls it but super(), and that every class defining it redefines the field with it as default (else Odoo would not run that override, and the hook would). kwargs: the keyword arguments the hand implementation takes (src/orm/private_hooks.ts PrivateKwargs, the last of its args): a compiled super() passes those names to it as keywords; another keyword argument goes into its place among the positional ones (compiler/oc/build.py hand_params) or refuses. The hand port passes keyword arguments to a compiled override the same way, as a trailing PrivateKwargs.
